evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County lists Oenothera speciosa among plants occurring naturally and not introduced.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes multiple Oenothera speciosa specimens.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Oenothera speciosa.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county occurrence inferred from statewide native status; named counties are supported by explicit local/herbarium/project occurrence evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the flower architecture: a large, open, radial four-petaled primrose—usually pink to white—with 8 stamens and a conspicuous 4-lobed cross/finger-like stigma on a spreading rhizomatous plant.
diagnostic_traits: young shoots rosetted; later stems decumbent to ascending
large radial flowers about 25–52 mm across
4 broad fan- to heart-shaped pink/white petals

confusers.separator: Both can have large primrose flowers, but O. triloba is a flat, essentially stemless rosette with yellow flowers borne on an extremely long square floral tube; O. speciosa has leafy stems and a much shorter tube.
O. speciosa has a broad radial flower with four spreading petals; O. lindheimeri has the airy 'gaura' look with petals held mainly to the upper side and long projecting stamens.
